name: a-one-lane-half-slice-fills-an-rgba16float-texel-with-zeros
rationale: DESIGN D495: Metal writes an imageblock slice's lanes and then zeros whatever the texture's format (EVs TIB-slice-m4, TIB-slice-m3). Each 4x4 threadgroup fills its explicit imageblock's half cells with (1 + x + 8y)/64 at grid position (x, y), and its first thread writes the 1-lane slice at the threadgroup's first grid position into an 8x8 RGBA16Float texture first filled with 0x5A bytes: every texel becomes (v, 0, 0, 0). The translator filled the other channels with the lane before D495.

name: a-one-lane-half-slice-lands-in-the-rg16float-texture-an-argument-buffer-names
rationale: DESIGN D495: the slice of A written to the texture an argument buffer at slot 0 names, whose format the function cannot know when it compiles; the translator refused it before D495 (the slice's format was a pipeline fact). The texture is an 8x8 RG16Float first filled with 0x5A bytes: every texel becomes (v, 0), Metal's lanes then zeros (EVs TIB-slice-m4, TIB-slice-m3).

name: a-two-lane-short-slice-fills-an-rgba16sint-texel-with-zeros
rationale: DESIGN D495 in the integer class: each cell holds short2(x - 3, -100y - 7) at grid position (x, y), and the 2-lane slice lands in an 8x8 RGBA16Sint texture first filled with 0x5A bytes as (x - 3, -100y - 7, 0, 0), Metal's lanes then zeros in every format (EVs TIB-slice-m4, TIB-slice-m3).

name: fragment-varying-half4-with-viewport
rationale: The fragment returns its perspective center half4 varying unchanged while structurally accepting an unused viewport index; the generated fullscreen draw captures the color byte-exactly.

name: carry-a-signed-max-texel-to-its-tonemapping-output
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.read_texture_2d.i16.s.v4i32 (21 case-less sources), the ushort2-coordinate signed-int texel read. The kernel is straight-line: it reads texel (0,0) of the min and the max input textures and copies each to two outputs, so one thread and one texel per texture is the whole behaviour. The compared output is outputTonemappingMaxTexture, which carries the SECOND read -- a lowering that read the first texture twice, or that mixed the two reads up, lands on the min texel instead. Min is (-5, 0, 7, -128) and max is (11, -22, 33, 127): disjoint in every lane, signed on both sides of zero, and every value inside int8 so the answer does not depend on the storage width the writes are lowered at.

name: linked-single-unit-scan-min
rationale: One invocation and one thread execute one scan element with unit source, destination, and intermediate extents. Every loop bound and elements-per-thread field is one, the axis is zero, and the four-byte threadgroup allocation holds the single float lane before one exact destination write.

name: linked-single-radix13-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-13 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: copy-one-of-thirteen-selected-matrix-pairs-through-two-permutations
rationale:
Thirteen source buffers and thirteen destination buffers are selected in a pair of parallel select cascades keyed on thread_position_in_grid.z, then passed to an impl helper the frontend did not inline, so the two selected DEVICE POINTERS cross a call boundary that Logical SPIR-V has no pointer value for. The dispatch is 4x4x13 threads in 4x4x1 threadgroups, so z takes every one of the thirteen values and no collapse of either cascade to a single arm survives: the observed destination is buffer 21, the z=7 arm, and a chain that always picks the first or the last arm reads a different source buffer whose sixteen bytes are all different.

Both function constants are on, which turns on the two permutation loads: a byte is read at the UNPERMUTED (x, y) and written at (colPerm[x], rowPerm[y]), and the guard tests the PERMUTED coordinates against the per-matrix bounds in members 7 and 8, so the sixteen writes are a scattered subset of the thirty-two candidates and the two slices land in disjoint halves of the destination. Sixteen of the thirty-two destination bytes are written and sixteen keep a distinct initial fill, so a stray write names the byte it hit. The row and column bounds and the destination strides live in [13 x ...] arrays indexed by that same z, so a wrong index into them changes which writes pass the bound.

execution_safety is authored_bounded: the AIR has exactly one CFG cycle, the impl helper's slice loop, which counts from zero and exits when the counter equals params member 4 (byte 216). The manifest authors that member as 2, and the preceding `== 0` early-out is therefore not taken, so every invocation runs exactly two iterations. The three guards ahead of it -- x unsigned-less-than member 2 (byte 208, authored 4), y unsigned-less-than member 3 (byte 212, authored 4) -- pass for all sixteen threads of every threadgroup, so no invocation returns before the loop.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bin
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element; the exact callback is loop-free and returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. The one-bin histogram parameters force every active scalar lane to bin zero, and the poisoned counter makes the bounded global-atomic write observable byte-exactly.

name: argmin-two-rows-of-ten-signed-chars-an-unsigned-accumulator-gets-wrong
rationale:
No authored case reached `llvm.smin.i8`, which 3 corpus sources use; this kernel is MLX's `arg_reduce_general<char, ArgMin, 4>` and the call IS its running minimum, so its answer decides both output words. The case runs two rows of ten with `ndim` 1, `shape` (2), `in_strides` (10), `out_strides` (1), `axis_stride` 1 and `axis_size` 10: two threadgroups of thirty-two threads, so threads 0..31 reduce row 0 -- where `gid < lsize` short-circuits `elem_to_loc` and both offsets are 0 -- and threads 32..63 reduce row 1, where both index loops actually run. Each thread reads four consecutive axis elements, so with an axis of ten only threads 0, 1 and 2 see real data and the other twenty-nine see nothing but the identity the out-of-range guard supplies.

Signedness is the case, and its counterfactual is stated exactly: the running accumulator is the only thing `llvm.smin.i8` decides -- the index test beside it and the comparison in the cross-lane reduction are `icmp` and stay signed whatever the call lowers to. Simulating this kernel with the accumulator replaced by an unsigned minimum and everything else unchanged answers indices 2 and 7 where the correct lowering answers 4 and 3. Both rows separate, and they separate differently: row 0 is -3, 1, -2, 2, -7, 3, -5, 9, 8, 6, mixed-sign small values whose minimum is 7 at index 4 while the unsigned minimum latches onto a negative early; row 1 is -7, 100, -120, -128, 0, 1, -128, -5, 3, -12, where the true answer is the first of two equal extrema. Row 1's repeat -- -128 at indices 3 and 6 -- is also the tie rule: the per-thread scan advances its index only on a STRICT improvement and the simd reduction prefers the smaller index on an equal value, so 3 is the only correct answer and 6 is exactly what a non-strict comparison gives.

The extrema sit in different threads' four-element windows -- row 0's in thread 1, row 1's in thread 0 with a runner-up in thread 1 -- so the cross-lane `air.simd_shuffle_down.s.i8` pair reduction has to run for either row to come out right. The input buffer carries four elements past the two rows that the `axis_size` guard must never read. The output buffer is four words and only two are written; the other two must keep their 0x9C poison. `execution_safety` is `authored_bounded`: the AIR has six CFG cycles -- two `elem_to_loc` walks bounded by `ndim` = 1, the block loop bounded by ceil(axis_size / 4*lsize) = 1, two four-element inner loops, and the two shuffle reductions bounded by log2(simd_size) = 5.

name: nan-model-arithmetic-of-nan-operands-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_arith's program and lanes compiled with the default fast math: fadd, fsub, fmul, fdiv fast, air.fma fast, the contracted a * b + c, air.fast_sqrt, air.fast_fmod. A NaN operand is undefined under fast math; this records what Metal answers. Compiled without fast math unless named; every operand is loaded from a buffer, so nothing folds but what the AIR shows. NaN operands: quiet and signaling of either sign with payloads 0, 1, 2, 0x1000, 0x155555, 0x2aaaaa, 0x3ffffe, 0x3fffff. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: a-mesh-function-reads-its-payload-past-its-own-type
rationale: mesh_outputs_triangles, which declares a 16-byte payload element and reads four, under a generated object function whose 64-byte payload holds four float4 positions: Metal sizes the payload by the object function's type, so its two covering triangles draw the primitive data pc (1, 1) over a 2x2 RGBA32Float target.

name: compare-two-device-element-pointers-for-equality
rationale: Comparing two DEVICE POINTERS is done by 324 corpus sources and no authored case had ever exercised it. Logical SPIR-V pointers are not values, so the translator cannot compare addresses: emit_icmp_ptr_resolved has to answer from the access-chain INDEX PATHS instead, through emit_provenance_pointer_icmp / normalized_pointer_icmp_provenance / flatten_pointer_icmp_provenance / provenance_root_local_name / emit_pointer_index_equality -- 295, 295, 26, 26 and 24 corpus sources, all previously uncased. Both comparisons here are between two pointers into the SAME buffer with DIFFERENT index expressions, which is what makes them index comparisons rather than a null test. p = &buf[gid] against q = &buf[(gid >> 1) << 1] is equal on even lanes only, and the two indices are distinct SSA values, so the answer has to come from a runtime OpIEqual and not from spotting the same id twice. p against the fixed &buf[3] is a dynamic index against a constant one. Each comparison is combined with a real load through the pointer, so the buffer is genuinely bound and a comparison folded to a constant is visible as an offset of exactly 100 or 1000. buf = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128), all exact binary32, so the answer is (101, 2, 104, 8, 116, 32, 164, 128) then (1008, 1008, 1008, 8, 1008, 1008, 1008, 1008). An inverted predicate swaps the 100s onto the odd lanes; a comparison folded true adds 100 or 1000 everywhere; one folded false adds it nowhere. The AIR is hand-written because the corpus hosts are large and none of them can be driven to exact bytes.

name: atomics-past-a-device-buffer
rationale: Eight threads (DESIGN D225, the buffer atomic form). ctr is 12 words: counters 0x100, 0x200, 0x300, 0x400, then eight result words. idx = 0, 1, 2, 3, 12, 13, 40, 75. Thread t adds 1 + t to ctr[idx[t]] and stores the returned value to ctr[4 + t]: threads 0 to 3 add to one counter each, so ctr[0..4] = 0x101, 0x202, 0x303, 0x404 and ctr[4..8] = 0x100 to 0x400; threads 4 to 7 add past ctr's 48 bytes (words 12 to 75, within its 256-byte reach), whose returned values Metal leaves undefined: ctr bytes 32 to 47 are the declared out-of-bounds reads of ctr. Nothing outside ctr changes.

name: fused-multiply-add-and-ten-exact-conversions
rationale:
One invocation covering eleven uncovered families that are all exactly derivable: air.fma.v3f32, the three 64-bit integer conversions, four narrowing or widening conversions, saturate on half2, trunc on float2 and ldexp. They are 132 corpus sources between them and every corpus host reaches them only from a loop or a gated region. Every operand is read from a buffer, so none of it constant-folds in the front end.

The three fma lanes are the point of the case. Each takes a = 1 + 2^-23 scaled by a power of two, b = 1 - 2^-24 and c the negation of the rounded product, so the exact product is 1 + 2^-24 - 2^-47 scaled by that same power of two. Adding c to the rounded product gives exactly zero -- the excess is just under half an ulp, so it rounds away -- while adding it to the exact product gives 2^-24 - 2^-47, 2^-23 - 2^-46 and 2^-22 - 2^-45, each of which float32 holds exactly. A lowering that emits a multiply and an add instead of one fused operation writes three zeros; anything correctly fused writes those three values, which are more than twenty binades away from zero and unmistakable.

The rest is chosen so no rounding decision is involved at all. The unsigned 64-bit values are 1, 1024, 3*2^40 and 2^62 and the signed ones are their negatives and zero: all have at most two significant bits, so the widening to float32 is exact, and 1e10 is 2^10 times 9765625, which float32 holds exactly, so truncating it back to a 64-bit integer is exact in both directions and covers a magnitude no 32-bit path could carry. The half-to-int pair truncates towards zero from both signs; the ushort-to-half triple ends at 2048, the largest power of two below half's integer limit; the uint-to-ushort triple is 65535, 65536 and 70000, which pins the modulo rather than a saturation; the float-to-short quadruple ends exactly at 32767 and -32768, the two endpoints of the range. saturate is given a value below zero, one above one and two strictly inside, so both clamps and the pass-through are all observed.

name: linked-k24-two-row-quantized-vector-matrix
rationale: Reaching variant of linked-zero-k cases of this entry (DESIGN D296), whose parameters stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes; the user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). The parameters select two rows of x (vec_n_rows 2 in the user constant) against W's row 0 over K = 24: lanes 0 to 5 each dequantize four 8-bit values per row, the simdgroup sums each row, and lane 0 hands both rows' results to the linked destination callback, which writes them in turn to element index threadgroup_position.x = 0 of table entry 1 (4 bytes observed: the second row's result). x holds 1 to 5 repeating (so the two rows differ), the scales 0.5, 1, 2 repeating, the biases 0 to 3 repeating, and W small integers below 16, so every product and partial sum is an integer multiple of 0.5 far below 2^24: exact in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-vector-matrix

name: implicit-lod-sample-through-a-texture-selected-per-fragment
rationale: A fullscreen draw into a 16x16 rgba32_float target. Each fragment selects texture a when its position's x exceeds 8 and b otherwise, then samples the selected texture with implicit level of detail at pos.xy / 16 through a runtime sampler that is nearest, not mipmapped, and clamps to edge (sampler.sample_hoisted_grad.switch: the gradients are hoisted before the switch, DESIGN D19, D213). Both textures are 16x16 of one level, so the sample at the centre of pixel (x, y) is texel (x, y) of the chosen texture, whatever the derivatives: a's texel is (x, y, 1, 0.5) and b's (100 + x, 100 + y, 2, 0.25), so columns 8..15 read a and 0..7 read b. The observation is the whole target, initially 0xab. The AIR has no loop.

name: blend-eight-packed-normals-by-powers-of-two
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.convert.f.v4f32.s.v4i16, the short4 -> float4 conversion at the centre of this kernel packed-normal decode. maxIndex is 1 and the grid is one thread, so invocation 0 is the whole answer. Each delta w word is bitcast to uint and cut into three signed 10-bit fields, and every field is either +511 or -511, whose product with the 1/511 scale is exactly +1.0 or -1.0 in binary32 -- so the converted lanes are exact and the fast variant has nowhere to differ. The eight weights are 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128, so every partial sum is a small exact integer and the fast-math reassociation the module permits cannot change the result whatever order the eight terms are added in. outN = (1+2+4+8+16+32+64+128, 1-2+4-8+16-32+64-128, 1+2+4+8-16-32-64-128) = (255, -85, -225). Field 3 of every packed word is zero and field 2 is never zero, which keeps each w word a NORMAL binary32 -- this module compiles with denorms disabled.

name: visible-table-clear-slot-two-dual-output
rationale: One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body. Eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds, with register 2 selected as the result. This entry swizzles that result to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and selects binding zero for byte-exact comparison.

name: sign-the-saturated-depth-blend-of-a-clamped-window
rationale:
One invocation at gid (0, 0) over an eight-by-one forward and backward pair. The window bounds make air.max.s.i32 and air.min.s.i16 do real work: the low bound is max(0, 0 - 3) = 0, and the high bound is min(width - 1, 0 + 3), where the two operands are 7 and 3, so a min that answered with the wrong operand would average eight texels instead of four. The four texels inside the window all hold forward and backward (0.5, -0.5), so each contributes min(1, -0.5 + -0.5) - min(1, 0.5 + 0.5) = -1 - 1 = -2, and the four outside hold (-0.5, 0.5) and would contribute +2 each. The average over the correct window is therefore exactly -2; over the whole row it would be 0, which the sign at the end turns into zero rather than a magnitude, so the two answers are not near each other. Every intermediate -- 0.5, 1, -2, -4, -6, -8 and the count 1 through 4 -- is exact in binary16.
The blend is sign(d) * (0.5 * tanh(15 * (|d| - 0.25)) + 0.5). With d = -2 the tanh argument is 26.25, and in binary16 tanh rounds to exactly 1.0 once 1 - tanh(x) falls below 2^-12, past about 4.51 -- so the half transcendental has one representable answer whichever approximation runs, and the blend is exactly 1. air.sign.f16 is what turns it into the written -1: a sign that answered +1 for a negative argument, or dropped the multiply, writes +1 in all four channels instead.
air.fmin.f16 is exercised on both sides of its clamp -- the y sum is below one and the x sum is at it -- but the saturation that makes tanh exact also swallows a dropped fmin here, so this case does not pin it.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-six-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 6 and receives exact float4 zero from all five linked _uber_clear bodies. An eight-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x1 resource.

name: surface-shadow-zero-constants
rationale: The clipping helper's only backedge exits at an unsigned 16-bit counter value of 32, so one fragment invocation executes at most 32 loop iterations.

name: float4-to-half4-varying-conversion
rationale: The generated companion supplies a finite float4 perspective varying; the fragment converts every lane to half and writes the result byte-exactly.

name: bounded-dynamic-visible-table-clear-slot-two-2x1-output
rationale: The literal four-word size table [4, 0, 0, 0] bounds the only reachable loop: its induction starts at visible-table slot 2, increments once to 3, and exits because the masked first word minus one is exactly 3. One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body without dereferencing callback arguments. Eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds. This entry writes a 2x1 block at primary-texture origin (2,0); the 4x1 poisoned resource contains that full footprint, which is selected for byte-exact comparison.

name: gather-copy-three-sparse-page-table-entries-by-index
rationale: No authored case reached `llvm.memcpy.p1.p2.i64`, the constant-to-device fixed-length block copy that eight corpus sources use; this kernel is the smallest of them at 90 lines and does nothing else, so every output byte is that memcpy's. The kernel reads `opsCount` from the args buffer and then, for each op, copies the 16-byte page-table entry at `sourcePageTable[op.sourcePageIndex]` over `destPageTable[op.destinationPageIndex]`. The three ops are the permutation (src 2 -> dst 0, src 0 -> dst 2, src 1 -> dst 1), so the destination is a shuffle of the source, not a prefix of it: a lowering that copied from the wrong operand, ignored the index GEPs, or used a source-ordered walk would produce the identity instead and be visible in the first sixteen bytes. The three source entries are `(0x1122334455667788, 1)`, `(0xDEADBEEF, ~0)` and `(0x0102030405060708, 1<<63)` -- byte-asymmetric within each ulong and distinct across entries, so a byte-swapped, half-length, or 8-byte-only copy all differ from the expected bytes. The destination is a fourth entry longer than any op names and starts as 0xAB poison, so the tail proves the copy is bounded by the op list and does not run past the last written entry. Address space 2 is `constant` and address space 1 is `device`, which is the pointer pair this memcpy spelling exists to name, and the 16-byte length and align-8 operands are the ABI as the frontend wrote them. The dispatch is a single thread because the kernel takes no thread-position argument and every thread would redundantly perform the same copies. `execution_safety` is `authored_bounded`: the AIR loop is a real CFG cycle whose trip count is `opsCount`, read from buffer 0, which this case pins to 3.

name: nine-exact-integer-and-half-intrinsics-in-one-dispatch
rationale: An owned fixture that calls nine exact integer and half intrinsics once each and writes one result word per intrinsic, so a wrong lowering names itself by which word moved. It covers air.reverse_bits.i32, which is the highest-reach uncovered family in the corpus at 146 sources and which no corpus host can pin: every one of them uses it as the radical inverse inside a 1024-iteration Monte-Carlo integration over fast transcendentals. air.rotate.i32 is blocked the same way. A fixture removes that constraint because the value reaches the output directly. Each input was chosen to discriminate: the clamp input has its high bit set, so the unsigned clamp pulls it DOWN to 0x30000000 while a signed one would push it UP to 0x20000000; the median is taken over 7, -3 and 2 so the answer is neither the smallest nor the largest; the max is over -5 and -9 so an unsigned max would answer -9; and the rotate amount of eight moves 0x92345678 to 0x34567892, which is wrong under a right rotate. The other families covered are air.popcount.v4i32, air.clamp.u.v2i32, air.fmedian3.f16, air.ctz.i16, air.max.s.i16 and the two half converts the median needs.

name: patch-draws-a-kernel-encodes-at-factor-scales-and-the-host-encodes
rationale: Patch draws in an indirect command buffer that allows patch draws alone (DESIGN D336, D317 part 5g), each run by the post-tessellation template (token 1, inherited, with the marks buffer the execution binds at vertex index 0): every domain point stores 0x10000 | instance << 8 | patch at its cell of grid instance * 8 + patch. Triangle factor structures of buffer 2: 1, 1, 2, 1. Producer thread 0: patches at positions 1 and 2 with indices 5 and 6 (from the second device index), two instances from 1, factors from the second structure on (2 and 1), scale 1. Thread 1: patch index 2 (constant), instance 3, constant factors 1, scale 2: factors of 2. Thread 2: patch 0, instance 4, factors 1, scale 0.5, which integer partitioning rounds up to 1. Threads 3, 4, 5: scales 0, -1 and NaN, instances 5 to 7: nothing (D317 item 19, measured on an M4). The host encodes command 6: patches at positions 0 and 1 with indices 3 and 4 (buffer 1 from byte 16), one instance, factors from byte 8 of buffer 2 (1 and 2). Expected nonzero words: 75: 0x10003, 79: 0x10003, 95: 0x10003, 100: 0x10004, 102: 0x10004, 104: 0x10004, 106: 0x10004, 110: 0x10004, 112: 0x10004, 120: 0x10004, 325: 0x10105, 327: 0x10105, 329: 0x10105, 331: 0x10105, 335: 0x10105, 337: 0x10105, 345: 0x10105, 350: 0x10106, 354: 0x10106, 370: 0x10106, 525: 0x10205, 527: 0x10205, 529: 0x10205, 531: 0x10205, 535: 0x10205, 537: 0x10205, 545: 0x10205, 550: 0x10206, 554: 0x10206, 570: 0x10206, 650: 0x10302, 652: 0x10302, 654: 0x10302, 656: 0x10302, 660: 0x10302, 662: 0x10302, 670: 0x10302, 800: 0x10400, 804: 0x10400, 820: 0x10400; every other word stays 0.
